cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset (dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3), saving 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms).

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. "Co-op rollback netcode prototype" was abandoned by dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b, because re-running tides every rollback frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff. "Shader compile cache and build farm" is completed: it built the shared content-addressed compile cache (dec-build-a-content-addressed-shader-compile-cache-s--e65rq9439k7xz5zh), with its key finally set by dec-key-the-shader-cache-on-preprocessed-source-defi--3a05ff0r954vxh30. I did not find an explicit closing record for it.

netcode-004.answer: Rollback was abandoned because it must re-run the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame, costing 4.8 ms on Skiff (about a fifth of the 25 ms frame), and the workarounds failed: quarter-resolution tide re-simulation desynced peers within 90 seconds, and leaving tides out of the snapshot breaks the bit-for-bit tide constraint (decision dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). That reason depends on the world Decision dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e (Run the tide simulation in 32.32 fixed point).

ports-012.answer: Because saltglass caustics shimmered badly at the 540p floor (visible in 7 of 10 dune views vs 2 of 10 at 576p), so decision dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb raised the floor to 576p (at +1.3 ms, still within the 33.3 ms budget); per fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q. (That decision was later superseded by a 504p floor.)

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Decision dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9 (derived from fnd-alpha-tested-foliage-costs-2-1-ms-in-the-visibil--f3g34x2k6fs367eb) moved them out because alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward, and saltglass can't live in the buffer since it refracts the resolved scene and needs that image first, so both render in a forward pass after the resolve.

render-032.answer: Per dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e: Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping it on two platforms would break the one-upscaler-on-every-platform Constraint. Owning Tern's code also lets the team change the upscaler quickly for saltglass refraction and caustics, with no vendor tickets or license to negotiate, even though Tern costs 0.7 ms more on Meridian.

render-046.answer: dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4 was reopened because the cost finding that sank virtual shadow maps was a capture error (with cached pages VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascades), and cascade seams through saltglass remain unsolved under cascaded shadow maps (dec-use-cascaded-shadow-maps-with-four-cascades--s5c1y9jaf275afzr).

render-047.answer: Decision dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1 returned Skiff to the visibility buffer because the release-build capture showed it at 7.4 ms versus 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), and keeping two opaque paths cost about one engineer-week a month in fixes, so the Skiff forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping.

world-036.answer: dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h: 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack (unreadable fiber stacks blocked crash triage for beta), and a continuation-wait thread pool kept workers 93% busy vs 95% for fibers, so fibers gave only two points of utilisation at the cost of unreadable crashes and the Gull thread-local bug.

world-051.answer: Float tides drifted apart across machines within 6 minutes (fnd-float-tides-drift-apart-between-machines-within--znd0wy18bfw2prss) from FMA contraction plus a Skiff sin() differing by one ulp, and the constraint requires bit-identical tide state on every peer; dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e chose 32.32 fixed point because integer math and a build-time sine table give identical bits on any CPU/compiler with no platform math library involved. The graph does not record an explicit evaluation of strict IEEE mode.

world-055.answer: dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew: the cold-cache rerun showed only the 4 MB dictionary losing to Zstandard on Skiff, so Kelp stays with a 1 MB dictionary, which cold on Skiff beats Zstandard by 1.7x (it decodes at 2.2 GB/s), closing the reopened Zstandard option.
